cards.explanation: The answer is as bold as a lion. The proverb says, “…the righteous are as bold as a lion.” The wicked are over there sprinting with nobody behind them. The righteous get a lion's boldness.

The answer is True. The proverb says a land in rebellion has many rulers, “…but a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.” Many rulers sit on one side, and one man of understanding and knowledge sits on the other. Order is what he maintains. Good news for any land.

The answer is no food. The proverb says a destitute leader who oppresses the poor is “…like a driving rain that leaves no food.” You'd expect rain to help the crops. This rain comes down hard and leaves nothing to eat.

The answer is those who seek the LORD. The proverb says, “Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD comprehend fully.” Notice who gets named: those who seek the LORD, with no fancy title attached. Evil men are on one side, and those who seek Him are on the other.

The answer is integrity, friends. “Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a rich man whose ways are perverse.” The proverb looks at how a man walks, not what he owns. A poor man with integrity is the one it calls better.

The answer is False. The proverb says, “…a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.” The other son in the verse is the discerning one, and “A discerning son keeps the law…” Which son would you rather be?

The answer is True. The proverb says, “He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.” The verse names who that wealth is laid up for. It's the one who is kind to the poor.

The answer is that he falls into his own pit. The proverb says, “He who leads the upright along the path of evil will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit what is good.” The pit is his own. I'd rather not be that guy.

The answer is a poor man with discernment. The proverb says, “A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees through him.” Being wise in your own eyes is easy. A poor man with discernment looks right through it.

The answer is hide. The proverb says, “When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.” Same idea shows up again at the end, in verse 28. When the wicked rise, people duck.

The answer is mercy, friends. The proverb says, “He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy.” Notice there are two parts: confessing and renouncing. Mercy is waiting for the one who does both.

The answer is hardens. The proverb says, “Blessed is the man who is always reverent, but he who hardens his heart falls into trouble.” Dough that sits out gets hard and cracks. A hard heart ends up in trouble.

The answer is a wicked ruler over a helpless people. The proverb says, “Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.” A lion in verse 1 is the picture of boldness. Here it's about a wicked ruler, and a charging bear comes along too.

The answer is True. The proverb says, “…he who hates dishonest profit will prolong his days.” A leader who lacks judgment is also a great oppressor. The one who hates dishonest profit is the one who prolongs his days.

The answers are safe for the first blank and fall for the second. The proverb says, “He who walks with integrity will be kept safe…” Integrity is the road that keeps a man safe. It also says, “…whoever is perverse in his ways will suddenly fall.” Notice the word suddenly. It's right there in the verse.

The answer is poverty, friends. The proverb says, “The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.” The worker gets plenty of food. The dreamer gets his fill of the opposite.

The answer is True. The proverb says, “To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.” Even something small as a piece of bread can push a man to do wrong. The verse doesn't soften it.

The answer is False. The proverb says, “A stingy man hastens after wealth and does not know that poverty awaits him.” He hurries after wealth with no idea poverty is waiting. I'd call that a surprise nobody wants.

The answer is the one who rebukes. The proverb says, “He who rebukes a man will later find more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.” Notice the word later. A rebuke can sting today, and the favor comes afterward.

The answer is he who trusts in the LORD. The proverb says, “A greedy man stirs up strife, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.” Greed stirs the pot. Trusting in the LORD is what leads to prospering.

The answer is True. The proverb says, “Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but he who hides his eyes will receive many curses.” The first line is about the one who gives. The second is about the one who hides his eyes, and the verse says he will receive many curses.

The answer is flourish, friends. The proverb says, “When the wicked come to power, people hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.” We started this chapter with the wicked running. It ends with the righteous flourishing.
